subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Differentiate between meristematic and permanent tissues in plants. Discuss the various types of permanent tissues in detail.
answer_key: Meristematic tissues consist of actively dividing cells, lack vacuoles, have thin cellulose walls and dense cytoplasm, and are responsible for growth. Permanent tissues are formed from meristematic tissues after they lose the ability to divide, have definite shape and size, and perform specialized functions. Permanent tissues are classified into simple permanent tissues (parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma) and complex permanent tissues (xylem, phloem). Parenchyma provides storage and packaging; collenchyma provides mechanical support and flexibility; sclerenchyma provides rigidity and mechanical strength.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Explain the classification of animal epithelial tissues based on their structure and function. Give examples of where each type is found in the human body.
answer_key: Epithelial tissues form the covering or lining of most organs and cavities. They are classified into: 1. Squamous epithelium (thin, flat, delicate lining found in blood vessels, lung alveoli for selective transport); 2. Cuboidal epithelium (cube-like cells providing mechanical support, found in kidney tubules, salivary gland ducts); 3. Columnar epithelium (tall, pillar-like cells, often bearing cilia, found in the inner lining of the intestine and respiratory tract); 4. Stratified squamous epithelium (arranged in layers to prevent wear and tear, found in skin).

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Describe the structure and function of complex permanent plant tissues. How do xylem and phloem differ in their components and transport mechanisms?
answer_key: Complex permanent tissues are made of more than one type of cell working together to transport water, minerals, and food. Xylem consists of tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma, and xylem fibres; it conducts water and dissolved minerals upward from roots to leaves and provides mechanical strength. Phloem consists of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, and phloem fibres; it transports prepared food materials from leaves to other parts of the plant (bidirectional transport).

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: What are connective tissues? Explain the composition and specific roles of blood, bone, cartilage, and areolar tissue in the human body.
answer_key: Connective tissues bind, support, and pack other tissues or organs of the body. Their cells are loosely spaced in an intercellular matrix. 1. Blood: Liquid matrix (plasma) containing RBCs, WBCs, and platelets; transports gases, nutrients, and wastes. 2. Bone: Rigid, solid matrix rich in calcium and phosphorus; provides structural framework and protects vital organs. 3. Cartilage: Solid matrix of proteins and sugars with widely spaced cells; smoothens bone surfaces at joints and provides flexibility to nose/ears. 4. Areolar tissue: Loose connective tissue found between skin and muscles; fills space inside organs and supports internal organs.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Compare and contrast parenchyma, collenchyma, and sclerenchyma tissues in plants with respect to their cell walls, presence of intercellular spaces, and primary functions.
answer_key: 1. Parenchyma: Thin cell walls made of cellulose, large intercellular spaces present, living cells; functions in food storage, photosynthesis (chlorenchyma), and buoyancy in aquatic plants (aerenchyma). 2. Collenchyma: Thickened cell walls at the corners due to pectin deposition, little or no intercellular spaces, living cells; provides mechanical support and flexibility, allowing bending of plant parts without breaking. 3. Sclerenchyma: Thick cell walls uniformly thickened with lignin, dead cells with no intercellular spaces; provides extreme rigidity, mechanical strength, and protection (e.g., husk of coconut).

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Explain the detailed structure of a neuron with a description of how nerve impulses are transmitted across nervous tissue.
answer_key: Nervous tissue consists of neurons specialized for receiving and transmitting stimuli. A neuron has three main parts: 1. Cyton (cell body) containing nucleus and cytoplasm; 2. Dendrites (short, branched hair-like projections that receive signals); 3. Axon (a single long process that transmits impulses away from the cell body). Nerve impulses are electrical signals generated by chemical changes, traveling from dendrites through the cyton and down the axon to the nerve endings, from where they are passed to the next neuron across a synapse.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Classify muscular tissue into three major types. Compare them based on their structure, location, and whether they are voluntary or involuntary.
answer_key: Muscular tissue is responsible for movement in the body. It is classified into: 1. Skeletal (Striated) muscles: Long, cylindrical, unbranched, multinucleated with alternating light and dark bands; attached to bones; voluntary control; responsible for body movements. 2. Smooth (Unstriated) muscles: Spindle-shaped, uninucleated, lack striations; found in walls of stomach, intestine, blood vessels; involuntary control; moves food and regulates blood flow. 3. Cardiac muscles: Cylindrical, branched, uninucleated with intercalated discs; found exclusively in the heart wall; involuntary control; rhythmic contraction and relaxation throughout life without fatigue.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Explain the concept of cell differentiation in plants. How do apical, lateral, and intercalary meristems contribute to plant growth and tissue formation?
answer_key: Cell differentiation is the process by which cells derived from meristematic tissue take up a permanent shape, size, and function. Meristems are regions of active cell division in plants. 1. Apical meristem is located at the growing tips of roots and stems; it increases the height or length of the plant. 2. Lateral meristem (cambium) is located along the side of stems and roots; it increases the girth (thickness) of the plant. 3. Intercalary meristem is located at internodes or leaf bases (e.g., below nodes in grasses); it helps in the elongation of parts like leaves and stems.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Describe the protective tissues in plants. Explain the role of the epidermis, stomata, and cork in plant survival and defense against environmental stress.
answer_key: Protective tissues provide protection against loss of water, mechanical injury, and invasion by parasitic fungi. 1. Epidermis: Single outer layer of cells covering the entire plant, often secreted with a waxy, water-resistant layer (cuticle) to prevent water loss. 2. Stomata: Specialized epidermal cells enclosed by guard cells that regulate gaseous exchange and transpiration. 3. Cork: As plants age, outer protective tissue is replaced by secondary meristem producing cork cells impregnated with suberin, making them impervious to gases and water, protecting old stems and roots.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Analyze how animal tissues are structurally adapted for their specific physiological roles. Support your answer with examples covering epithelial, connective, muscular, and nervous tissues.
answer_key: Animal tissues show remarkable structural adaptations: 1. Epithelial tissues form compact, continuous sheets without intercellular spaces to act as efficient barriers and absorptive surfaces. 2. Connective tissues possess an extensive extracellular matrix containing fibers and specialized cells (e.g., calcium phosphate in bone, plasma in blood) to provide support, linkage, and transport. 3. Muscular tissues contain contractile proteins (actin and myosin) arranged in fibers that shorten upon stimulation, enabling locomotion and visceral movements. 4. Nervous tissues have elongated axons and dendrites with specialized membrane properties to rapidly conduct electrochemical signals over long distances across the body.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: What is the main function of meristematic tissue in plants? Where are apical meristems located?
answer_key: Meristematic tissues are actively dividing tissues responsible for plant growth. Apical meristems are located at the growing tips of roots and stems, and they help in increasing the length of the plant body.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Differentiate between parenchyma and sclerenchyma tissues based on their cell wall composition and cellular spacing.
answer_key: Parenchyma cells have thin cell walls made of cellulose and possess prominent intercellular spaces for gaseous exchange and storage. Sclerenchyma cells have thick, lignified cell walls with no intercellular spaces, providing mechanical strength and rigidity to the plant.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Why are plant tissues categorized into meristematic and permanent tissues? Explain briefly.
answer_key: Plant tissues are divided based on their dividing capacity. Meristematic tissues consist of cells that retain the ability to divide continuously, leading to growth. Permanent tissues are formed when meristematic cells lose their capacity to divide and take up specific shapes, sizes, and functions.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: What is the role of stomata in plant leaves, and which specialized cells surround them?
answer_key: Stomata are tiny pores on the epidermal surface of leaves responsible for gaseous exchange (oxygen and carbon dioxide) and transpiration (loss of water vapor). They are surrounded and regulated by specialized epidermal cells called guard cells.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Define epithelial tissue and name any two types of simple epithelium based on their cell shape.
answer_key: Epithelial tissue forms the protective covering and lining of most organs and cavities in animal bodies. Two common types of simple epithelium based on cell shape are squamous epithelium (flat and tile-like) and cuboidal epithelium (cube-like).

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Why is blood considered a type of connective tissue? Explain two of its main components.
answer_key: Blood is considered a connective tissue because it connects different body parts, transporting oxygen, nutrients, wastes, and hormones, and has cells embedded in an extracellular matrix. Its main components are plasma (the fluid matrix) and formed elements (RBCs, WBCs, and platelets).

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Differentiate between striated (skeletal) and cardiac muscles based on their location and contraction properties.
answer_key: Striated skeletal muscles are attached to bones, are voluntary in action, and fatigue easily. Cardiac muscles are found exclusively in the walls of the heart, are involuntary, striated, and contract rhythmically throughout life without fatigue.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: What are the structural components of a neuron (nerve cell)? State the function of the axon.
answer_key: A neuron consists of a cell body (cyton) containing a nucleus and cytoplasm, branching dendrites, and a long tail-like axon. The function of the axon is to conduct nerve impulses away from the cell body to other neurons or effector organs.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Explain the importance of the waxy layer of cutin present on the epidermis of desert plants.
answer_key: The waxy layer of cutin on the epidermal cells of desert plants forms a water-resistant barrier. This significantly reduces the rate of water loss through transpiration, helping the plant survive in dry, arid environments.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: How does nervous tissue transmit messages across the body? Give a brief overview.
answer_key: Nervous tissue is composed of neurons that are specialized for receiving stimuli and conducting electrical impulses rapidly across the body. Dendrites receive signals, convert them into electrical impulses that travel along mandatorily through the axon, and transmit them via chemical or electrical signals at synapses to adjacent neurons or target tissues.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: A student observes epidermal cells of an onion peel under a compound microscope with a 10X eyepiece and a 40X objective lens. If the image of a cell appears 0.8 mm wide under total magnification, calculate the actual width of the epidermal cell in micrometers (microns).
answer_key: Total magnification = Eyepiece magnification * Objective magnification = 10 * 40 = 400X. Actual width = Apparent width / Total magnification = 0.8 mm / 400 = 0.002 mm. Converting millimeters to micrometers (1 mm = 1000 micrometers): 0.002 mm * 1000 = 2 micrometers. Final answer: 2 micrometers.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: In an apical meristem tissue sample, a single meristematic cell undergoes mitosis and divides every 30 minutes. Starting with 5 initial cells, calculate the total number of cells produced after 3 hours, assuming 100 percent survival and continuous division.
answer_key: Total time in minutes = 3 hours * 60 minutes/hour = 180 minutes. Number of division cycles (n) = Total time / Generation time = 180 / 30 = 6 divisions. Total cells = Initial cells * (2^n) = 5 * (2^6) = 5 * 64 = 320 cells. Final answer: 320 cells.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: To determine the Stomatal Index (SI) of a leaf epidermal peel, a researcher counts 45 epidermal cells and 5 stomata in a microscopic field. Calculate the Stomatal Index percentage using the formula: SI = [S / (E + S)] * 100, where S is the number of stomata and E is the number of epidermal cells.
answer_key: Formula: SI = [S / (E + S)] * 100. Substituting values: SI = [5 / (45 + 5)] * 100 = [5 / 50] * 100 = 0.1 * 100 = 10%. Final answer: 10%.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: A plant tissue sample weighing 50 g fresh weight is dried in an oven and its dry weight is found to be 10 g. Out of this dry weight, sclerenchyma (dead thick-walled mechanical tissue) accounts for 65% by mass. Calculate the total mass of living parenchyma and collenchyma cells combined in the dried sample.
answer_key: Dry weight of sample = 10 g. Mass of sclerenchyma = 65% of 10 g = 0.65 * 10 = 6.5 g. Mass of living cells (parenchyma + collenchyma) = Total dry weight - Mass of sclerenchyma = 10 g - 6.5 g = 3.5 g. Final answer: 3.5 g.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Water moves upward through the xylem tissue of a plant stem at a uniform velocity of 2.5 cm per minute. Calculate the total vertical distance (in meters) the water column travels through the xylem in 4 hours.
answer_key: Time in minutes = 4 hours * 60 minutes/hour = 240 minutes. Total distance in cm = Velocity * Time = 2.5 cm/min * 240 min = 600 cm. Converting centimeters to meters (1 m = 100 cm): 600 cm / 100 = 6 meters. Final answer: 6 meters.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: In a prepared slide of mammalian blood (fluid connective tissue), a blood smear shows an average count of 5,000 Red Blood Cells (RBCs) per small counting grid square. If the volume of blood represented by one grid square is 0.0002 cubic millimeters, calculate the concentration of RBCs per cubic millimeter of blood in standard scientific notation.
answer_key: RBC concentration per cubic millimeter = Number of RBCs / Volume of grid square in mm^3 = 5000 / 0.0002 = 5000 / (2 * 10^-4) = 25,000,000 = 2.5 * 10^7 cells/mm^3. Final answer: 2.5 * 10^7 cells per cubic millimeter.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: A plant stem cross-section exhibits a vascular bundle in which the phloem tissue occupies an area of 0.15 mm^2 and the xylem tissue occupies 0.45 mm^2. Calculate the ratio of phloem area to total vascular bundle area (xylem + phloem) expressed as a percentage.
answer_key: Total vascular bundle area = Xylem area + Phloem area = 0.45 + 0.15 = 0.60 mm^2. Ratio of phloem area = (Phloem area / Total area) * 100 = (0.15 / 0.60) * 100 = 0.25 * 100 = 25%. Final answer: 25%.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: During a laboratory experiment to stain plant tissues, a student needs 50 mL of a 2% (w/v) safranin solution. Calculate the mass of solid safranin powder (in grams) required to prepare this solution.
answer_key: A 2% (w/v) solution means 2 grams of solute in 100 mL of solution. Mass of solute = (Percentage / 100) * Volume = (2 / 100) * 50 = 0.02 * 50 = 1 gram. Final answer: 1 gram.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: A striated muscle tissue fiber (skeletal muscle) undergoes a rapid contraction cycle where it shortens in length by 15% from its relaxed length of 80 micrometers. Calculate the contracted length of the muscle fiber in micrometers.
answer_key: Reduction in length = 15% of 80 micrometers = (15 / 100) * 80 = 12 micrometers. Contracted length = Relaxed length - Reduction = 80 - 12 = 68 micrometers. Final answer: 68 micrometers.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: A bone tissue sample (hard supportive connective tissue) has a total dry weight of 200 g. If inorganic mineral salts (mainly calcium and phosphorus compounds) account for 70% of the bone's dry weight and the remaining percentage consists of organic matrix (collagen fibers), calculate the total mass of the organic matrix in grams.
answer_key: Percentage of organic matrix = 100% - 70% = 30%. Mass of organic matrix = 30% of 200 g = (30 / 100) * 200 = 0.30 * 200 = 60 g. Final answer: 60 g.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question:
Read the passage below and answer the questions that follow: 
During a practical class, Riya observed a cross-section of a plant stem under a microscope. She noticed actively dividing cells at the root and shoot tips, characterized by dense cytoplasm, thin cellulosic cell walls, and prominent nuclei. Further down the stem, she observed cells that had lost the ability to divide and had taken up specific shapes and functions.
(a) Name the specific plant tissue found at the root and shoot tips.
(b) Why do these cells possess dense cytoplasm and prominent nuclei but lack vacuoles?
(c) What is the process by which dividing cells take up permanent shape, size, and function called?
answer_key:
(a) Meristematic tissue (specifically apical meristem).
(b) They possess dense cytoplasm and prominent nuclei because they are actively involved in cell division and metabolic activity. They lack vacuoles because vacuoles store water and waste, which would hinder rapid division and cytoplasmic density in meristematic cells.
(c) Differentiation.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question:
Read the passage below and answer the questions that follow:
Aman visited a botanical garden and touched the flexible petiole of a leaf, which bent easily without breaking. He also observed the rough, hard outer covering of a coconut shell. The guide explained that these properties are due to different types of simple permanent tissues in plants.
(a) Identify the plant tissue responsible for flexibility in the leaf petiole.
(b) Identify the plant tissue responsible for the hardness of the coconut shell.
(c) State one major structural difference between the cells of these two tissues regarding cell wall thickening.
answer_key:
(a) Collenchyma.
(b) Sclerenchyma.
(c) Collenchyma cells are unevenly thickened at the corners due to pectin deposition, whereas sclerenchyma cells have uniform thickenings heavily deposited with lignin, making them dead and rigid.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question:
Read the passage below and answer the questions that follow:
Water and minerals absorbed by roots must reach the topmost leaves of a tall tree, while food manufactured in leaves needs to be distributed to all plant parts. Plants achieve this through complex permanent tissues.
(a) Name the two components of complex permanent tissues in plants.
(b) Which element of the water-conducting tissue is dead at maturity?
(c) Explain why phloem transport is bidirectional unlike xylem transport.
answer_key:
(a) Xylem and Phloem.
(b) Xylem vessels and tracheids (or xylem fibres).
(c) Xylem transports water and minerals upward from roots to leaves (unidirectional). Phloem transports synthesized food from leaves (source) to storage organs or growing regions (sink), which can be upward or downward depending on plant needs, hence bidirectional.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question:
Read the passage below and answer the questions that follow:
In an animal tissue slide demonstration, a teacher showed squamous epithelium lining the blood vessels and lung alveoli, while columnar epithelium lined the inner surface of the intestine with microvilli.
(a) Why is squamous epithelium also known as pavement epithelium?
(b) What is the primary function of squamous epithelium in lung alveoli?
(c) How do microvilli on columnar epithelial cells assist in the intestine?
answer_key:
(a) Squamous epithelium consists of extremely thin and flat cells that fit closely together like tiles on a floor, hence called pavement epithelium.
(b) It facilitates easy exchange of gases (oxygen and carbon dioxide) through selective diffusion.
(c) Microvilli increase the surface area for efficient absorption of digested food nutrients in the intestine.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question:
Read the passage below and answer the questions that follow:
Connective tissues bind different tissues/organs and provide structural support. Blood, bone, cartilage, tendon, and ligament are examples of connective tissues with specialized fluid or solid matrices.
(a) What is the intercellular matrix of blood called, and what is its composition?
(b) Differentiate between a tendon and a ligament based on what they connect.
(c) Why is bone matrix hard while cartilage matrix is flexible?
answer_key:
(a) Plasma; it is composed of water, proteins, salts, and hormones.
(b) Tendons connect skeletal muscles to bones, whereas ligaments connect bone to bone.
(c) Bone matrix is embedded in rigid calcium and phosphorus compounds, whereas cartilage has a solid matrix composed of proteins and sugars providing flexibility.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question:
Read the passage below and answer the questions that follow:
Muscular tissue is responsible for movement in our body. Muscle cells are elongated and known as muscle fibres. They contain contractile proteins that cause contraction and relaxation.
(a) Name the three types of muscular tissues found in animals.
(b) Which muscle type is under conscious will and shows alternate light and dark bands?
(c) Why do cardiac muscles never fatigue throughout a person's life?
answer_key:
(a) Striated (skeletal) muscles, unstriated (smooth) muscles, and cardiac muscles.
(b) Striated (skeletal) muscles.
(c) Cardiac muscles are involuntary, branched cells with abundant mitochondria and rich blood supply that allow rhythmic contraction and relaxation without fatigue.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question:
Read the passage below and answer the questions that follow:
Nervous tissue is specialized for transmitting stimuli rapidly from one part of the body to another. The functional unit of this tissue is highly specialized with a cell body, dendrites, and an axon.
(a) What is the structural and functional unit of nervous tissue called?
(b) What is the role of dendrites in impulse transmission?
(c) Define synapse and mention its role in neural communication.
answer_key:
(a) Neuron (or nerve cell).
(b) Dendrites receive electrical impulses/signals from other neurons or sensory receptors and transmit them toward the cell body (cyton).
(c) A synapse is the junction between the axon terminal of one neuron and the dendrites of the next neuron, where chemical neurotransmitters pass the impulse across.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question:
Read the passage below and answer the questions that follow:
Plant outer surfaces are covered by protective tissues to prevent loss of water, mechanical injury, and invasion by parasitic fungi. The epidermis is typically a single layer of cells covered by a waxy, waterproof layer.
(a) Name the waxy, waterproof secretion found on the outer walls of epidermal cells in desert plants.
(b) What are the tiny pores present in the epidermis of leaves called, and what are their two main functions?
(c) How does cork tissue provide protection in older woody stems/trees?
answer_key:
(a) Cuticle.
(b) Stomata; functions are gaseous exchange and transpiration of water.
(c) Cork cells are dead, compactly arranged without intercellular spaces, and impregnated with suberin, making them impervious to gases and water, protecting against mechanical injury and pathogens.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question:
Read the passage below and answer the questions that follow:
Plant tissues differ fundamentally from animal tissues due to their sedentary lifestyle compared to active locomotion in animals. This dictates distinct energy and tissue requirements.
(a) Why do plants require more dead tissues compared to animals?
(b) Which plant tissue provides mechanical support without adding weight and is living?
(c) Give two broad categories into which plant permanent tissues are classified.
answer_key:
(a) Plants are stationary and need structural strength to withstand severe environmental forces (wind, rain) without requiring active maintenance energy, so dead supporting tissues (like sclerenchyma and xylem) are advantageous.
(b) Collenchyma.
(c) Simple permanent tissues and Complex permanent tissues.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question:
Read the passage below and answer the questions that follow:
During an investigation into animal connective tissues, students examined adipose tissue and areolar tissue. They noted that adipose tissue stores fat and acts as an insulator, whereas areolar tissue fills spaces inside organs and supports internal organs.
(a) Where is adipose tissue predominantly located in mammals?
(b) Why is areolar tissue referred to as 'packing tissue' of the body?
(c) Name the cells found in areolar tissue that help in repairing damaged tissues.
answer_key:
(a) Below the skin and between internal organs.
(b) Because it fills the space inside organs, supports internal organs, and helps in repairing tissues, packing various structures together.
(c) Fibroblasts, mast cells, and macrophages.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: The shortest distance measured from the initial position to the final position of an object is known as ___.
answer_key: Displacement. Displacement is a vector quantity representing the straight-line distance between the initial and final positions.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: The rate of change of displacement with respect to time is called ___.
answer_key: Velocity. Velocity is defined as displacement per unit time and includes both magnitude and direction.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: In a velocity-time graph, the area under the curve represents the ___ covered by the object.
answer_key: Displacement. The product of velocity and time (area under v-t graph) gives the total displacement of the moving object.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: When an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, however small the intervals may be, the motion is said to be ___ motion.
answer_key: Uniform. Uniform motion describes an object moving at a constant speed along a straight line.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: The SI unit of acceleration is ___.
answer_key: m/s² (or metre per second squared). Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, measured in meters per second per second.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Slope of a distance-time graph at any given point gives the instantaneous ___ of the object.
answer_key: Speed. The slope of the distance-time graph represents the rate of change of distance, which is speed.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only

answer_key: Opposite. Deceleration means velocity is decreasing, so the acceleration acts in the direction opposite to the velocity.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: The numerical ratio of displacement to distance for a moving object is always less than or equal to ___.
answer_key: One (or 1). Since displacement is the shortest path and distance is the actual path length, displacement is always less than or equal to distance.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: For an object in uniform circular motion, its speed remains constant, but its ___ changes continuously.
answer_key: Velocity (or direction of motion). In circular motion, the direction changes at every point, making velocity change even if speed is constant.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only

(B) Non-uniform motion
(C) Uniform motion
(D) Impossible motion physically
answer_key: Correct matching: 1-C (An inclined straight line on a distance-time graph represents uniform motion), 2-A (A line parallel to the time axis indicates the distance is not changing with time, meaning the object is at rest), 3-B (A curved line represents non-uniform motion), 4-D (A line parallel to the distance axis implies infinite speed in zero time, which is physically impossible). Therefore, 1-C, 2-A, 3-B, 4-D.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Distinguish between distance and displacement with respect to a moving body.
answer_key: Distance is the total length of the actual path covered by a body between initial and final positions, and it is a scalar quantity. Displacement is the shortest straight-line distance between the initial and final positions of the body, and it is a vector quantity.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Under what condition is the magnitude of average velocity of an object equal to its average speed?
answer_key: The magnitude of average velocity is equal to average speed when an object moves in a straight line in a single direction without turning back, so the total path length (distance) is equal to the magnitude of displacement.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Define acceleration and state its SI unit. When is acceleration considered positive?
answer_key: Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity with respect to time. Its SI unit is meter per second squared (m/s^2). Acceleration is considered positive when the velocity of an object increases with time.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: What does the slope of a distance-time graph represent for a moving object? Explain.
answer_key: The slope of a distance-time graph represents the speed of the object. A steeper slope indicates a higher speed, while a straight horizontal line parallel to the time axis indicates that the object is at rest (zero speed).

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Can an object have zero velocity and still be accelerating? Give an example.
answer_key: Yes, an object can have zero instantaneous velocity while still accelerating. For example, when a ball is thrown vertically upwards, at its highest point of motion, its instantaneous velocity becomes zero for an instant, but it is still acted upon by acceleration due to gravity, which is directed downwards.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Explain the difference between uniform motion and non-uniform motion in a straight line with suitable examples.
answer_key: Uniform motion occurs when an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, no matter how small the time intervals are (e.g., a car moving at a constant speed of 60 km/h on a straight highway). Non-uniform motion occurs when an object covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time, or equal distances in unequal intervals (e.g., a car moving through heavy city traffic).

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: What do you infer about the motion of an object whose velocity-time graph is a straight line parallel to the time axis?
answer_key: A velocity-time graph that is a straight line parallel to the time axis indicates that the object is moving with constant or uniform velocity. Its acceleration is zero because the velocity does not change with time.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: How can you find the distance travelled by an object from its speed-time (or velocity-time) graph?
answer_key: The distance travelled by an object can be found by calculating the area enclosed under the speed-time (or velocity-time) graph and the time axis between the given initial and final time instances.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Differentiate between speed and velocity. Mention any two points of distinction.
answer_key: 1. Speed is the rate of change of distance (scalar quantity), whereas velocity is the rate of change of displacement (vector quantity). 2. Speed can never be negative or zero for a moving body, whereas velocity can be positive, negative, or zero depending on the direction of motion.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Explain why uniform circular motion is considered an accelerated motion even though the speed of the object remains constant.
answer_key: Uniform circular motion is accelerated motion because acceleration depends on a change in velocity. In circular motion, even though the magnitude of speed remains constant, the direction of motion continuously changes at every point along the circular path. Since velocity is a vector (having both magnitude and direction), a change in direction results in a change in velocity, thereby producing acceleration (centripetal acceleration).

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: A car travels a distance of 120 km in 3 hours. Calculate its average speed in m/s.
answer_key: Average speed = Total distance / Total time = 120 km / 3 h = 40 km/h. Converting km/h to m/s by multiplying by 5/18: 40 * (5/18) = 200/18 = 11.11 m/s.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: A bus starting from rest moves with a uniform acceleration of 0.1 m/s² for 2 minutes. Find (a) the speed acquired, and (b) the distance travelled.
answer_key: Given initial velocity u = 0, acceleration a = 0.1 m/s², time t = 2 min = 120 s. (a) Speed acquired v = u + at = 0 + (0.1 * 120) = 12 m/s. (b) Distance travelled s = ut + 0.5 * a * t^2 = 0 + 0.5 * 0.1 * (120)^2 = 0.05 * 14400 = 720 m.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: A train is travelling at a speed of 90 km/h. Brakes are applied so as to produce a uniform acceleration of -0.5 m/s². Find how far the train will go before it is brought to rest.
answer_key: Initial velocity u = 90 km/h = 90 * (5/18) = 25 m/s. Final velocity v = 0. Acceleration a = -0.5 m/s². Using v^2 = u^2 + 2as: 0 = (25)^2 + 2(-0.5)s => 0 = 625 - s => s = 625 m.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: A trolley, while going down an inclined plane, has an acceleration of 2 cm/s². What will be its velocity 3 s after the start?
answer_key: Initial velocity u = 0 (since it starts from rest), acceleration a = 2 cm/s², time t = 3 s. Using v = u + at: v = 0 + (2 cm/s² * 3 s) = 6 cm/s (or 0.06 m/s).

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: A stone is thrown in a vertically upward direction with a velocity of 5 m/s. If the acceleration of the stone during its motion is 10 m/s² in the downward direction, what will be the height attained by the stone and how much time will it take to reach there?
answer_key: Initial velocity u = 5 m/s, acceleration a = -10 m/s² (downward), final velocity v = 0 at maximum height. (1) Time t: v = u + at => 0 = 5 + (-10)t => t = 5/10 = 0.5 s. (2) Height s: v^2 = u^2 + 2as => 0 = (5)^2 + 2(-10)s => 20s = 25 => s = 1.25 m.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: An athlete completes one round of a circular track of diameter 200 m in 40 s. What will be the distance covered and the displacement at the end of 2 min 20 s?
answer_key: Diameter d = 200 m, radius r = 100 m. Time for one round T = 40 s. Total time t = 2 min 20 s = 140 s. Number of rounds n = 140 / 40 = 3.5 rounds. Distance covered = 3.5 * circumference = 3.5 * (2 * (22/7) * 100) = 2200 m. At the end of 3.5 rounds, the athlete is at the diametrically opposite point, so displacement equals the diameter = 200 m.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: A motorboat starting from rest on a lake accelerates in a straight line at a constant rate of 3.0 m/s² for 8.0 s. How far does the boat travel during this time?
answer_key: Initial velocity u = 0, acceleration a = 3.0 m/s², time t = 8.0 s. Distance s = ut + 0.5 * a * t^2 = 0 + 0.5 * 3.0 * (8.0)^2 = 1.5 * 64 = 96 m.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: A particle is moving in a circle of radius r. What is the magnitude of the displacement and distance covered after completing half of the circle?
answer_key: Radius = r. Distance covered in half circle = half of the circumference = pi * r. Displacement in half circle = straight-line distance between initial and final points = diameter = 2r.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Two cars A and B start from rest at the same time from the same point in the same direction. Car A moves with a uniform acceleration of 1.2 m/s² while car B moves with a uniform acceleration of 1.0 m/s². Find the distance between them after 10 seconds.
answer_key: Initial velocity u = 0 for both. For car A: acceleration a1 = 1.2 m/s², time t = 10 s. Distance sA = 0.5 * a1 * t^2 = 0.5 * 1.2 * (10)^2 = 60 m. For car B: acceleration a2 = 1.0 m/s², time t = 10 s. Distance sB = 0.5 * a2 * t^2 = 0.5 * 1.0 * (10)^2 = 50 m. Distance between them = sA - sB = 60 - 50 = 10 m.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: A car accelerates uniformly from 18 km/h to 54 km/h in 5 seconds. Calculate (a) the acceleration of the car, and (b) the distance covered by the car in that time.
answer_key: Initial velocity u = 18 km/h = 18 * (5/18) = 5 m/s. Final velocity v = 54 km/h = 54 * (5/18) = 15 m/s. Time t = 5 s. (a) Acceleration a = (v - u) / t = (15 - 5) / 5 = 10 / 5 = 2 m/s². (b) Distance s = ut + 0.5 * a * t^2 = (5 * 5) + 0.5 * 2 * (5)^2 = 25 + 25 = 50 m.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Which of the following represents a homogeneous mixture?
options: A mixture of oil and water
A mixture of chalk powder and water
answer_key: Salt dissolved in water is a homogeneous mixture because its composition is uniform throughout the solution. The other options are heterogeneous mixtures.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Which method is best suited for separating a mixture of two miscible liquids whose boiling point difference is more than 25°C?
answer_key: Simple distillation is used for separating miscible liquids with a boiling point difference greater than 25°C. Fractional distillation is used when the difference is less than 25°C.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: An immiscible liquid mixture of oil and water can be best separated using which of the following apparatus?
answer_key: A separating funnel is used to separate immiscible liquids. They separate into layers based on their densities, with the denser liquid at the bottom.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Which of the following mixtures shows the Tyndall effect?
answer_key: Milk is a colloid, and colloids scatter a beam of light passing through them, exhibiting the Tyndall effect. True solutions (like salt, copper sulphate, and sugar solutions) do not show this effect.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: The principle behind the process of centrifugation is:
options: Denser particles are forced to the bottom and lighter particles stay at the top when spun rapidly
Difference in boiling points of components
Selective adsorption on a stationary phase
answer_key: Centrifugation works on the principle that denser particles are forced to the bottom and lighter particles stay at the top when subjected to high-speed rotation.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Which of the following changes represents sublimation?
answer_key: Sublimation is the transition of a substance directly from the solid to the gas state without passing through the liquid state.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: During the separation of a mixture of ammonium chloride and common salt, the substance that sublimes and collects on the inverted funnel is:
answer_key: Ammonium chloride is a sublimable solid. When heated, it vaporizes directly and condenses on the cooler parts of the inverted funnel, leaving common salt behind.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Chromatography is primarily used to separate:
options: Components of a mixture that dissolve in the same solvent
Solid-solid mixtures of different particle sizes
answer_key: Chromatography is used to separate solutes that dissolve in the same solvent but have different affinities or rates of movement through a stationary phase.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: A solution in which no more solute can be dissolved at a specific temperature is known as a:
answer_key: A saturated solution is one that contains the maximum amount of solute that can be dissolved in a given solvent at a specified temperature.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Which of the following techniques is most appropriate to separate colored components from a sample of ink?
answer_key: Ink is a mixture of a dye in water. Paper chromatography is used to separate the different colored components present in the dye based on their differential solubility.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: The process of separating a mixture of two or more miscible liquids by heating them followed by condensation is known as ___.
answer_key: Distillation. Explanation: Distillation is used for the separation of components of a mixture containing two miscible liquids that boil without decomposition and have sufficient difference in their boiling points.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: A solution in which no more solute can be dissolved at a specific temperature is called a ___ solution.
answer_key: Saturated. Explanation: At any particular temperature, a solution that has dissolved as much solute as it is capable of dissolving is said to be a saturated solution.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: The scattering of a beam of visible light by colloidal particles is called the ___ effect.
answer_key: Tyndall. Explanation: The Tyndall effect is exhibited when a beam of light passes through a colloid, making the path of light visible due to scattering by colloidal-sized particles.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: The technique used to separate cream from milk is ___.
answer_key: Centrifugation. Explanation: Centrifugation works on the principle that the denser particles are forced to the bottom and the lighter particles stay at the top when rapidly spun, commonly used to separate cream from milk.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: Two miscible liquids with a boiling point difference of less than $25^\circ\text{C}$ can be separated using ___ distillation.
answer_key: Fractional. Explanation: Fractional distillation uses a fractionating column packed with glass beads to provide surfaces for vapors to cool and condense repeatedly, separating liquids with close boiling points.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: The process of conversion of a solid directly into gas without passing through the liquid state is ___.
answer_key: Sublimation. Explanation: Sublimation is the transition of a substance directly from the solid to the gas state, utilized to separate sublimable volatile components from non-sublimable impurities.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: The technique used for separation of colors present in a dye is ___.
answer_key: Chromatography. Explanation: Chromatography is the technique used for separation of those solutes that dissolve in the same solvent, such as different pigments from an extract of flower petals.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: The random zigzag movement of colloidal particles in a dispersion medium is called ___ motion.
answer_key: Brownian. Explanation: Brownian motion refers to the continuous, chaotic, zigzag motion of colloidal particles resulting from collisions with molecules of the dispersion medium.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: The method used to separate pure solid crystals from an impure solution is ___.
answer_key: Crystallization. Explanation: Crystallization is a process that separates a pure solid in the form of its crystals from a solution, which is superior to simple evaporation because it avoids decomposition.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
seed_question: A mixture of two immiscible liquids like oil and water can be separated using a ___ funnel.
answer_key: Separating. Explanation: Immiscible liquids separate out in layers depending on their densities. A separating funnel allows the denser layer to be drained out first while leaving the lighter layer behind.

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only

subject: Science (Exploration) - Class 9 only
