subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: What is the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha as per the Constitution of India?
answer_key: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is constitutionally fixed at 552 members (530 from states, 20 from Union Territories, and previously 2 Anglo-Indian members nominated by the President, though the nomination for Anglo-Indians was discontinued via the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Who presides over a joint sitting of both Houses of the Indian Parliament?
answer_key: According to Article 108 of the Constitution, a joint sitting of both Houses is summoned and presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. In the absence of the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker presides, and in their absence, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: What is the term of office for a member of the Rajya Sabha (Upper House)?
answer_key: Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected for a term of 6 years. One-third of its members retire every two years, making it a permanent body that is not subject to dissolution.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Which of the following bills can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha and not in the Rajya Sabha?
answer_key: A Money Bill (defined under Article 110) deals exclusively with financial matters such as taxation, borrowing, and the Consolidated Fund of India. It can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the President.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: What is the minimum age requirement for a person to contest elections for membership to the Lok Sabha?
answer_key: To be chosen as a member of the Lok Sabha, a person must not be less than 25 years of age. For the Rajya Sabha, the minimum age requirement is 30 years.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Under which Article of the Constitution can the Rajya Sabha pass a resolution empowering Parliament to make laws on a matter enumerated in the State List?
answer_key: Under Article 249, if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting that it is necessary in the national interest, Parliament becomes competent to make laws on subjects in the State List.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: What fraction of the total members of the Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha constitutes the quorum to transact business?
answer_key: The quorum to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament is one-tenth (1/10th) of the total number of members of that House as per Article 100(3).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: How many members are nominated by the President to the Rajya Sabha from persons having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art, and social service?
answer_key: The President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha who possess special knowledge or practical experience in fields such as literature, science, art, and social service.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Who certifies whether a particular bill is a Money Bill or an Ordinary Bill?
answer_key: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha has the sole and final authority to certify whether a bill is a Money Bill under Article 110(3). This decision is final and cannot be questioned in any court.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: What is the maximum gap allowed between two consecutive sessions of Parliament?
answer_key: According to Article 85(1) of the Constitution, the President shall summon each House of Parliament to meet at such time and place that six months shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: The Union Parliament of India consists of the President, the Lok Sabha, and the ___.
answer_key: Rajya Sabha. Explanation: According to Article 79 of the Constitution of India, the Parliament consists of the President and two Houses known respectively as the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha as prescribed by the Constitution is ___ members.
answer_key: 250. Explanation: Under Article 80 of the Constitution, the maximum seating capacity/strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250 members, out of which 238 represent states and union territories, and 12 are nominated by the President.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: The ___ is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
answer_key: Vice-President. Explanation: According to Article 64 and Article 89(1) of the Constitution, the Vice-President of India acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: A Money Bill can be introduced only in the ___.
answer_key: Lok Sabha. Explanation: Under Article 110 and Article 109 of the Indian Constitution, a Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the President, giving the Lower House financial supremacy.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: The minimum age required for a person to contest elections for membership to the Lok Sabha is ___ years.
answer_key: 25. Explanation: Article 84(b) of the Constitution specifies that a candidate contesting for a seat in the Lok Sabha must not be less than 25 years of age.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution, with one-third of its members retiring every ___ years.
answer_key: two. Explanation: Under Article 83(1), the Rajya Sabha is not subject to dissolution, and nearly one-third of its members retire upon the expiration of every second year.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: A joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament to resolve a legislative deadlock is summoned by the ___.
answer_key: President. Explanation: Under Article 108 of the Constitution, the President of India summons a joint sitting of both Houses when a deadlock occurs over a non-money bill.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: The quorum to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament is ___ of the total number of members of that House.
answer_key: one-tenth. Explanation: According to Article 100(3) of the Constitution, the quorum for a meeting of either Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha is one-tenth of the total members of the House.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: The maximum gap allowed between two consecutive sessions of Parliament cannot exceed ___ months.
answer_key: six. Explanation: Article 85(1) of the Constitution mandates that Parliament must meet at least twice a year, and the gap between two sessions cannot exceed six months.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: The power to decide whether a bill is a Money Bill or not rests exclusively with the ___ of the Lok Sabha.
answer_key: Speaker. Explanation: Under Article 110(3) of the Constitution, the decision of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha as to whether a bill is a Money Bill is final.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: State the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha and name its presiding officer.
answer_key: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 550 members. Its presiding officer is called the Speaker.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: What is the normal term of the Lok Sabha? Under what circumstance and by whom can it be dissolved before its term expires?
answer_key: The normal term of the Lok Sabha is 5 years. It can be dissolved before its term expires by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister, or if the ruling party loses its majority and no alternative government can be formed.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Who presides over the meetings of the Rajya Sabha in the absence of the Vice-President of India?
answer_key: In the absence of the Vice-President (who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha), the meetings are presided over by the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, who is elected by the members of the House from amongst themselves.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: How are the members of the Rajya Sabha elected? Mention their total strength.
answer_key: Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies using the system of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote. The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250 members.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Why is the Rajya Sabha called a permanent House? State the tenure of its members.
answer_key: The Rajya Sabha is called a permanent House because it is not subject to dissolution as a whole. Instead, one-third of its members retire every two years, ensuring continuity. The tenure of an individual member is 6 years.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Mention any two qualifications required for a person to be chosen as a member of the Lok Sabha.
answer_key: Any two qualifications for a member of the Lok Sabha are: 1. Must be a citizen of India. 2. Must not be less than 25 years of age. (Alternative: Must possess such other qualifications as may be prescribed by Parliament and not hold any office of profit).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: What is meant by the 'Quorum' of the Lok Sabha? State the minimum number of members required to constitute it.
answer_key: Quorum refers to the minimum number of members required to be present in the House to transact any official business. The quorum for the Lok Sabha is one-tenth of the total membership of the House (i.e., 55 members).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: State two exclusive powers of the Lok Sabha that are not enjoyed by the Rajya Sabha.
answer_key: Two exclusive powers of the Lok Sabha are: 1. A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha. 2. A Motion of No-Confidence against the Council of Ministers can only be introduced and passed in the Lok Sabha.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Mention two special powers of the Rajya Sabha under the Indian Constitution (other than Money Bills).
answer_key: Two special powers of the Rajya Sabha are: 1. It can declare a subject in the State List to be of national importance by passing a resolution supported by a two-thirds majority (Article 249). 2. It can recommend the creation of one or more All-India Services common to the Union and the States (Article 312).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: What is meant by a 'Money Bill'? Where can it be introduced in the Parliament?
answer_key: A Money Bill is a financial bill that deals exclusively with matters such as taxation, borrowing of money, expenditure, or receipt from the Consolidated Fund of India. It can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha upon the recommendation of the President.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: State any four exclusive powers of the Lok Sabha that are not enjoyed by the Rajya Sabha.
answer_key: The four exclusive powers of the Lok Sabha are: 1. Money Bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha has no power to reject or amend it (can only delay for 14 days). 2. A Motion of No-Confidence against the Council of Ministers can only be introduced and passed in the Lok Sabha. 3. In case of a deadlock between the two Houses on a ordinary bill, during a joint sitting presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, the Lok Sabha usually has a numerical advantage. 4. Under Article 352, if the Lok Sabha passes a resolution disapproving the continuance of a National Emergency, the President has to revoke it.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Explain three financial powers of the Union Parliament.
answer_key: The three financial powers of the Union Parliament are: 1. Passing the Annual Budget: The government cannot impose any tax or incur expenditure without the approval of Parliament. 2. Supplementary Grants: If the amount authorized for the current financial year is found to be insufficient, the Parliament sanctions supplementary grants. 3. Control over Consolidated Fund: All revenues received by the Government of India form part of the Consolidated Fund of India, and no money can be withdrawn from it without Parliamentary approval.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Discuss the composition of the Rajya Sabha with respect to its maximum strength, method of election of its members, and nominated members.
answer_key: Composition of the Rajya Sabha: 1. Maximum Strength: The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250 members. 2. Representation of States and Union Territories: Out of these, up to 238 members represent the States and Union Territories. Their representatives are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies through proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote. 3. Nominated Members: 12 members are nominated by the President from persons having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art, and social service.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Explain three legislative powers of the Union Parliament.
answer_key: Three legislative powers of the Union Parliament are: 1. Law Making on Union List and Concurrent List: Parliament has exclusive power to make laws on subjects enumerated in the Union List and can also make laws on subjects in the Concurrent List. 2. Ordinance Approval: It has the power to approve or disapprove ordinances promulgated by the President when Parliament is not in session. 3. Creation of New States or Alteration of Boundaries: Parliament can pass laws to form new States, alter the boundaries, or change the names of existing States by a simple majority.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Mention any three qualifications required for a person to be chosen as a member of the Lok Sabha.
answer_key: The qualifications required for a person to be a member of the Lok Sabha are: 1. Citizen: Must be a citizen of India. 2. Age: Must not be less than 25 years of age. 3. Voter: Must be a registered voter in any constituency in India. Additionally, must not hold any office of profit under the Government of India or any State government and must not be of unsound mind or an undischarged insolvent.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: State the special powers of the Rajya Sabha under Article 249 and Article 312 of the Indian Constitution.
answer_key: The two special powers of the Rajya Sabha are: 1. Power under Article 249: The Rajya Sabha can pass a resolution by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting, declaring that it is necessary in the national interest for Parliament to make laws on a matter enumerated in the State List. 2. Power under Article 312: The Rajya Sabha can pass a resolution by a two-thirds majority to empower Parliament to create one or more All-India Services common to both the Union and the States.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Explain the composition and tenure of the Lok Sabha.
answer_key: Composition: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 550 members, all directly elected from territorial constituencies across states and union territories. Tenure: The normal term of the Lok Sabha is 5 years from the date appointed for its first meeting. However, it can be dissolved earlier by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister. During a National Emergency, its term can be extended by Parliament for one year at a time.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Explain the process of how an Ordinary Bill is converted into an Act in the Indian Parliament.
answer_key: An Ordinary Bill passes through the following stages to become an Act: 1. First Reading: Introduction of the bill in either House of Parliament where its title and objectives are read. 2. Second Reading: Detailed discussion clause by clause, amendments are proposed and voted upon. 3. Third Reading: General debate on the bill as a whole; no amendments are allowed at this stage. 4. Transmission to the Second House: The bill goes through the same three readings in the second house. 5. Assent of the President: Once passed by both Houses, the bill is presented to the President for assent. Upon signing, it becomes an Act.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Mention three ways in which the Parliament exercises control over the Executive.
answer_key: Three ways in which the Parliament exercises control over the Executive are: 1. Question Hour and Zero Hour: Members can ask questions to ministers regarding government policies and administration, holding them accountable. 2. Adjournment Motion: This motion is moved to draw the attention of the House to a matter of urgent public importance, leading to a censure of the government's policy. 3. No-Confidence Motion: The Lok Sabha can remove the cabinet from power by passing a vote of no-confidence.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Describe the electoral functions and judicial powers of the Union Parliament.
answer_key: Electoral Functions: Elected members of both Houses of Parliament form part of the Electoral College for the election of the President of India and elect the Vice-President of India. Judicial Powers: 1. Impeachment: Parliament has the power to impeach the President for violation of the Constitution. 2. Removal of Judges: It can address the President for the removal of Supreme Court and High Court judges on grounds of proved misbehavior or incapacity. 3. Breach of Privilege: It can punish members or outsiders for breach of parliamentary privileges or contempt of the House.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question:

answer_key: Correct Match: 1-A, 2-B, 3-C, 4-D. Rationale: The maximum sanctioned strength of the Lok Sabha is 552, Rajya Sabha is 250, the normal term of the Lok Sabha before dissolution is 5 years, and the quorum required to transact business in either House is one-tenth (1/10th) of the total members.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question:

Column I:

answer_key: Correct Match: 1-B, 2-A, 3-D, 4-C. Rationale: The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over joint sittings of Parliament. The Leader of the Opposition must represent a party with at least 10% of total strength. The Prime Minister is the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question:
Match the types of Bills in Column I with their specific characteristics in Column II:

Column I:
1. Money Bill
2. Ordinary Bill

Column II:

C. Requires special majority in both Houses separately
D. Deals with revenue and expenditure under Article 117
answer_key: Correct Match: 1-A, 2-B, 3-C, 4-D. Rationale: Money Bills (Article 110) originate exclusively in the Lok Sabha with prior presidential recommendation. Ordinary bills can originate in either House. Constitutional Amendment Bills require a special majority in both Houses. Financial Bills deal with financial matters under Article 117.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question:
Match the legislative powers in Column I with the respective House possessing exclusive authority in Column II:

Column I:
1. Introduction of Money Bill
2. Creation of new All-India Services
3. Passing a No-Confidence Motion

Column II:
A. Exclusive power of Lok Sabha under Article 109
B. Exclusive power of Rajya Sabha under Article 312
C. Exclusive power of Lok Sabha against the Council of Ministers
D. Must originate in Rajya Sabha under Article 67(b)
answer_key: Correct Match: 1-A, 2-B, 3-C, 4-D. Rationale: Money Bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha. The creation of All-India Services requires a Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 312. No-Confidence Motions apply only to the Lok Sabha. Resolutions for the removal of the Vice-President must originate in the Rajya Sabha.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question:
Match the parliamentary terms related to sessions in Column I with their definitions in Column II:

Column I:
1. Summons
2. Prorogation
3. Dissolution
4. Adjournment

Column II:
A. Termination of a session of the House by the President

D. Suspension of a sitting of the House for a specific time or sine die
answer_key: Correct Match: 1-C, 2-A, 3-B, 4-D. Rationale: Summons is the calling of the House to meet. Prorogation terminates a session. Dissolution ends the life of the Lok Sabha. Adjournment suspends work during a sitting.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question:
Match the financial terms and instruments in Column I with their descriptions in Column II:

Column I:
1. Annual Financial Statement
2. Cut Motion
3. Vote on Account
4. Consolidated Fund of India

Column II:
A. The official Budget presented under Article 112
B. Tool used by opposition to express disapproval of government policy
C. Grant for advance expenditure before the budget is passed
D. Fund to which all revenues received by the Government are credited
answer_key: Correct Match: 1-A, 2-B, 3-C, 4-D. Rationale: The Annual Financial Statement is the constitutional name for the budget. Cut motions express policy disapproval. Vote on Account allows advance grants. The Consolidated Fund of India holds all government revenues.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question:
Match the parliamentary proceedings and rules in Column I with their correct description in Column II:

Column I:

answer_key: Correct Match: 1-A, 2-B, 3-C, 4-D. Rationale: Question Hour is the first hour of a sitting. Zero Hour starts immediately after. Bills pending in Lok Sabha lapse on dissolution, whereas bills pending solely in Rajya Sabha do not.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question:

answer_key: Correct Match: 1-A, 2-B, 3-C, 4-D. Rationale: Lok Sabha candidates must be at least 25 years old, Rajya Sabha candidates 30 years. Anti-defection provisions are under the Tenth Schedule. Holding an office of profit disqualifies a member.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question:
Match the executive control motions in Column I with their purpose in Column II:

Column I:

answer_key: Correct Match: 1-A, 2-B, 3-C, 4-D. Rationale: Censure motions censure specific ministerial policies. Adjournment motions address urgent matters. No-confidence motions target the entire ministry. Policy cut motions reduce budget demands to Re. 1.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)

answer_key: Correct Match: 1-A, 2-B, 3-C, 4-D. Rationale: PAC examines CAG reports. Estimates Committee reviews budget estimates for economies. Committee on Public Undertakings oversees PSUs. JPCs investigate specific legislative matters across both Houses.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Assertion (A): The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house and cannot be dissolved. Reason (R): One-third of its members retire every two years, ensuring continuity.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Assertion (A): A Money Bill can originate only in the Lok Sabha. Reason (R): Lok Sabha is directly elected by the people, giving it absolute financial supremacy over the Rajya Sabha.

Money Bills deal with taxation and expenditure; because the Lok Sabha represents the direct mandate of citizens, it holds exclusive authority to introduce Money Bills, while Rajya Sabha can only delay it for up to 14 days.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Assertion (A): The Speaker of the Lok Sabha decides whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not. Reason (R): The decision of the Speaker in certifying a Money Bill is final and cannot be questioned in any court of law.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)

While Article 312 grants Rajya Sabha the exclusive power to recommend the creation of All India Services, such a resolution must be passed by a special majority—specifically, not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting, not a simple majority.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Assertion (A): A Vote of No-Confidence against the Union Council of Ministers can be moved in either House of Parliament. Reason (R): The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Parliament as a whole.

Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
answer_key: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true. A Vote of No-Confidence can be moved ONLY in the Lok Sabha, because under Article 75(3), the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible solely to the Lok Sabha, which directly represents the electorate.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Assertion (A): The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is fixed at 550 members under the Constitution. Reason (R): Following the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, the provision for nominating two Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha was discontinued.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
answer_key: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A). The maximum sanctioned strength of Lok Sabha is 550 (530 from States and 20 from UTs). With the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2019 ceasing the nomination of Anglo-Indians, the effective maximum strength stands at 550.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: What is the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha as per the Constitution of India?
answer_key: 552. Explanation: Under Article 81 of the Constitution, the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 552 members (up to 530 members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the States, up to 20 members to represent the Union Territories, and not more than 2 members from the Anglo-Indian community nominated by the President, though the nomination for Anglo-Indians ceased via the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: What is the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha as laid down by the Constitution of India?
answer_key: 250. Explanation: Under Article 80 of the Constitution, the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250 members, out of which 238 represent the States and Union Territories, and 12 members are nominated by the President from persons having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art, and social service.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: What fraction of the total members of the Rajya Sabha retire every two years?
answer_key: 1/3 or One-third. Explanation: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house and is not subject to dissolution. However, one-third of its members retire on the expiration of every second year, ensuring continuity with members having a tenure of 6 years.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: What is the minimum age requirement prescribed by the Constitution for a person to be chosen as a member of the Lok Sabha?
answer_key: 25 years. Explanation: According to Article 84(b) of the Constitution of India, the minimum age for contesting and becoming a member of the Lok Sabha (House of the People) is 25 years.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: What is the minimum age requirement prescribed by the Constitution for a person to be chosen as a member of the Rajya Sabha?
answer_key: 30 years. Explanation: According to Article 84(b) of the Constitution of India, the minimum age required to become a member of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) is 30 years.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: What is the minimum number of members required to constitute the quorum to meet either House of Parliament under Article 100(3) of the Constitution?
answer_key: 1/10th or One-tenth. Explanation: Article 100(3) states that unless Parliament by law otherwise provides, the quorum to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament shall be one-tenth of the total number of members of the House.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: How many maximum number of nominated members can be appointed by the President to the Rajya Sabha for their distinguished contribution in art, literature, science, and social service?
answer_key: 12. Explanation: Under Article 80(1)(a) of the Constitution, the President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha who possess special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art, and social service.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: Within how many days must a Money Bill passed by the Lok Sabha be returned by the Rajya Sabha with its recommendations, failing which it is deemed passed by both Houses in the form originally passed by the Lok Sabha?
answer_key: 14 days. Explanation: Under Article 110 and Article 109 of the Constitution, the Rajya Sabha has restricted powers over Money Bills. It must return a Money Bill within 14 days from the date of its receipt, either with recommendations or without them.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: What is the normal duration or tenure (in years) of a single term for an elected member of the Rajya Sabha?
answer_key: 6 years. Explanation: Under Article 83(1) of the Constitution, the Rajya Sabha is not subject to dissolution, but each member has a tenure of 6 years, with one-third retiring every two years.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question: What is the normal full term (in years) of the Lok Sabha from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless dissolved earlier?
answer_key: 5 years. Explanation: Under Article 83(2) of the Constitution, the Lok Sabha, unless sooner dissolved, continues for 5 years from the date appointed for its first meeting, and no longer.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question:
Case Study: Read the excerpt below and answer the questions that follow:
During a parliamentary session, a heated debate arose regarding a bill concerning the creation of an All-India Service common to the Union and the States. Some members argued that since legislative subjects concerning state administration are primarily under state jurisdiction, the Rajya Sabha cannot interfere. However, the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha clarified the special constitutional powers vested in the Upper House under Article 312.

Based on this scenario and your knowledge of the Union Parliament:
(a) Identify the specific power of the Rajya Sabha highlighted in the case regarding All-India Services and mention the Article associated with it.
(b) State one other exclusive financial or legislative power enjoyed by the Rajya Sabha that the Lok Sabha does not possess.
(c) Explain why the Rajya Sabha is called a permanent house.
answer_key:
(a) The power highlighted is the exclusive power of the Rajya Sabha under Article 312 to declare by a resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting that it is necessary in the national interest to create one or more All-India Services.
(b) Under Article 249, the Rajya Sabha has the exclusive power to pass a resolution by a two-thirds majority empowering Parliament to make laws on a matter enumerated in the State List in the national interest. (Alternatively: Exclusive power under Article 67 to initiate a resolution for the removal of the Vice President).
(c) The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house because it is not subject to dissolution as a whole; one-third of its members retire every two years, and new members are elected to fill those vacancies, ensuring continuity in the legislative process.
rubric_keywords: one-third members retire every two years

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question:
Case Study: Read the excerpt below and answer the questions that follow:
An ordinary bill was passed by the Lok Sabha during the budget session. However, the Rajya Sabha withheld its approval for more than six months, suggesting several amendments that the Lower House was unwilling to accept. To resolve this legislative deadlock, the President decided to invoke a specific constitutional mechanism under Article 108.

Based on this scenario and your knowledge of the Union Parliament:
(a) Name the constitutional mechanism invoked by the President to resolve the deadlock between the two Houses.
(b) Who presides over the joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament according to the Constitution of India?
(c) Can a Money Bill ever be subjected to this specific mechanism? Give a reason for your answer.
answer_key:
(a) Joint Sitting of both Houses of Parliament (Article 108).
(b) The Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over the joint sitting of both Houses.
(c) No, a Money Bill cannot be subjected to a joint sitting. Reason: A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha has very limited powers over it (it can only delay it for a maximum of 14 days), so the question of a deadlock requiring a joint sitting does not arise.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question:
Case Study: Read the scenario and answer the questions that follow:
During a parliamentary proceeding, a Member of Parliament raised a serious issue regarding government policy without giving the mandatory prior notice of ten days, demanding an immediate response from the Prime Minister. The Speaker disallowed the question, explaining that such urgent matters requiring immediate attention must follow a specific parliamentary device that allows discussions on urgent public importance.

Based on this scenario and your knowledge of parliamentary procedures:
(a) Identify the parliamentary device referred to for discussing matters of urgent public importance that interrupts the normal business of the House.
(b) What is the usual time allotted for this device during a parliamentary sitting?
(c) State one objective of question hour in the Parliament.
answer_key:
(a) Adjournment Motion.
(b) Usually taken up at 4:00 PM or after the Question Hour, occupying at least two and a half hours for discussion.
(c) The objective of the Question Hour is to enable members to seek information from the ministers on matters of public interest, thereby maintaining legislative control over the executive.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question:
Case Study: Read the text and answer the questions below:
A Member of Parliament introduced a bill aimed at amending certain provisions of the Constitution relating to federal distribution of powers. The bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha, and the member emphasized that special voting procedures must be followed for its passage, unlike ordinary legislative bills.

Based on this scenario and your knowledge of the legislative process:
(a) What type of bill is described in this context based on its purpose?
(b) State the special majority required in each House of Parliament for passing a Constitutional Amendment Bill.
(c) Can a Constitutional Amendment Bill be passed through a joint sitting of Parliament in case of disagreement? Explain briefly.
answer_key:
(a) Constitutional Amendment Bill (under Article 368).
(b) A majority of the total membership of that House and a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members of that House present and voting.
(c) No, a Constitutional Amendment Bill cannot be passed through a joint sitting. Both Houses must pass the bill separately by the requisite special majority.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question:
Case Study: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow:
In the Lok Sabha, a controversy arose when an opposition member accused the government of financial misappropriation and demanded that the Union Budget be rejected entirely. The Speaker intervened to explain the significance of the budget and the specific motion required to pass or reduce grants.

Based on this passage and your understanding of the Lok Sabha:
(a) What term is officially used in the Indian Constitution for the Annual Financial Statement?
(b) Who has the final authority to decide whether a bill is a Money Bill or an ordinary bill?
(c) State one reason why the Lok Sabha is considered more powerful than the Rajya Sabha in financial matters.
answer_key:
(a) Annual Financial Statement (Article 112).
(b) The Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
(c) Money Bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha has no power to reject or amend a Money Bill (it can only delay it for up to 14 days).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question:
Case Study: Read the excerpt and answer the questions that follow:
During a parliamentary debate on national security, opposition members expressed a lack of confidence in the Council of Ministers. A formal motion was moved in the Lok Sabha, signed by the requisite 50 members, challenging the government's survival.

Based on this scenario and your knowledge of parliamentary control:
(a) Identify the specific motion moved in the Lok Sabha against the Council of Ministers.
(b) What is the consequence if this motion is successfully passed by a majority of members present and voting in the Lok Sabha?
(c) Can such a motion be introduced in the Rajya Sabha? Give a reason for your answer.
answer_key:
(a) No-Confidence Motion.
(b) If the No-Confidence Motion is passed, the entire Council of Ministers (including the Prime Minister) must resign, as the government loses its majority support in the Lower House.
(c) No, it cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha. Reason: Under Article 75(3), the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible only to the Lok Sabha, which represents the directly elected representatives of the people.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question:
Case Study: Read the scenario and answer the questions that follow:
A newly elected member of the Lok Sabha was taking her oath. During the orientation, she was informed about the quorum required to transact business in the House and the quorum required for committee meetings.

Based on this scenario and your knowledge of parliamentary terms:
(a) Define the term 'Quorum' in the context of the Indian Parliament.
(b) What is the constitutional quorum required for holding a meeting in either House of Parliament?
(c) Who determines the quorum if no rule is prescribed by the Constitution for parliamentary committees?
answer_key:
(a) Quorum refers to the minimum number of members required to be present in the House before it can transact any official business.
(b) One-tenth (1/10th) of the total members of each House.
(c) The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha or the Speaker of the Lok Sabha (or respective committee chairpersons as per rules).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question:
Case Study: Read the excerpt and answer the questions that follow:
The Parliament of India consists of the President and the two Houses—the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha. While discussing the legislative powers of Parliament, a student wondered why the President, who is not a member of either house, is considered an integral part of the Parliament.

Based on this context and your knowledge of the Union Legislature:
(a) Give two reasons why the President is considered an integral part of the Union Parliament.
(b) State the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha as per the constitutional provisions.
(c) How are the members of the Rajya Sabha elected or nominated?
answer_key:
(a) The President is an integral part because: (1) No bill passed by both Houses can become an act without the President's assent. (2) The President summons, prorogues Parliament, and dissolves the Lok Sabha.
(b) The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 550 members (530 from States and 20 from Union Territories).
(c) Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States (using proportional representation via single transferable vote) and 12 members are nominated by the President for their distinguished contribution in literature, science, art, and social service.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question:
Case Study: Read the case and answer the questions that follow:
During the winter session of Parliament, an urgent question was raised regarding a sudden economic crisis. A member wanted to draw the attention of the minister concerned without giving the standard long notice period, utilizing a specific short-notice procedure.

Based on this situation and your knowledge of parliamentary instruments:
(a) What is meant by a 'Starred Question'?
(b) How is a Starred Question answered in the House?
(c) What type of supplementary questions can be asked following an answer to a Starred Question?
answer_key:
(a) A Starred Question is one to which a member desires an oral answer on the floor of the House, distinguished by an asterisk mark.
(b) It is answered orally by the concerned minister during the Question Hour.
(c) Supplementary questions can be asked spontaneously by the members as follow-ups to the oral answer provided.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
seed_question:
Case Study: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow:
An ordinary bill originated in the Rajya Sabha and was passed by it. It was then transmitted to the Lok Sabha. However, due to political differences and the impending dissolution of the Lok Sabha, questions arose regarding the lapse of bills pending in Parliament.

Based on this scenario and your knowledge of the legislative procedure:
(a) Under what circumstances does a bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapse upon its dissolution?
(b) Does a bill pending in the Rajya Sabha which has not been passed by the Lok Sabha lapse when the Lok Sabha is dissolved? Give a reason.
(c) Mention any one discretionary or special power of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha ensuring neutrality and order in the House.
answer_key:
(a) A bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses when the Lok Sabha is dissolved, regardless of whether it originated in the Lok Sabha or was transmitted from the Rajya Sabha.
(b) No, a bill pending in the Rajya Sabha which has not been passed by the Lok Sabha does not lapse when the Lok Sabha is dissolved, because the Rajya Sabha is a permanent house.
(c) The Speaker decides whether a bill is a Money Bill or maintains order and decorum by casting a deciding vote (casting vote) in case of a tie.
rubric_keywords: Rajya Sabha bill does not lapse

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)

answer_key: The Electoral College for the President consists of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States (and UTs of Delhi and Puducherry). Nominated members do not vote.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: What is the maximum permissible time gap between two consecutive sessions of Parliament?
answer_key: Under Article 85 of the Constitution, the President summons each House of Parliament to meet at such time and place as he thinks fit, but six months shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution can the President promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session?
answer_key: Article 123 of the Indian Constitution grants the President the power to promulgate ordinances during the recess of Parliament, which have the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: Who appoints the Prime Minister of India?
answer_key: The Prime Minister is appointed by the President of India under Article 75. Conventionally, the leader of the majority party or coalition in the Lok Sabha is appointed as Prime Minister.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: To whom does the Union Council of Ministers collectively responsible?
answer_key: As per Article 75(3) of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, meaning they remain in office only as long as they enjoy the confidence of the majority of Lok Sabha members.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: What is the minimum age required for a person to be eligible for election as the President of India?

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: Which term describes the executive powers of the Union where all executive actions of the Government of India are formally taken in his name?
answer_key: Under Article 77, all executive actions of the Government of India are formally taken in the name of the President, who is the nominal head of the executive.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: By what process can the President of India be removed from office before the expiry of their term?

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: Who acts as the principal channel of communication between the President and the Council of Ministers?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
answer_key: Under Article 78, it is the duty of the Prime Minister to communicate to the President all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to administration and proposals for legislation, acting as the bridge between them.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: The executive head of the Indian Union is the ___.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)

seed_question: The Vice-President of India acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the ___.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: The Prime Minister is appointed by the ___.
answer_key: President. Explanation: Under Article 75 of the Constitution, the Prime Minister is appointed by the President, who conventionally invites the leader of the majority party or coalition in the Lok Sabha to form the government.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: Ordinances promulgated by the President under Article 123 must be approved by Parliament within ___ weeks from the date of its reassembly.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)

seed_question: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the ___.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: The formal impeachment procedure of the President of India can be initiated in ___.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: The President can nominate ___ members to the Rajya Sabha who have special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art, and social service.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: The emergency power to declare a National Emergency due to war, external aggression, or armed rebellion is vested in the ___.

Qualifications: (1) Must be a citizen of India, (2) Must have completed the age of 35 years, (3) Must be qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha, (4) Must not hold any office of profit under the Government of India or any State Government.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: Discuss the executive and legislative powers of the President of India.
answer_key: Executive Powers: (1) All executive actions of the Government of India are formally taken in the President's name. (2) The President appoints the Prime Minister and, on the advice of the Prime Minister, other Union Ministers. (3) The President appoints key constitutional officials such as the Attorney General, Comptroller and Auditor General, Governors of States, and Chief Justice and Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts. Legislative Powers: (1) The President summons and prorogues both Houses of Parliament and can dissolve the Lok Sabha. (2) The President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha with special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art, and social service. (3) No Bill passed by Parliament can become a law without the President's assent.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: Explain the emergency powers of the President of India, focusing on National Emergency and President's Rule.
answer_key: The President of India has emergency powers under three categories: (1) National Emergency (Article 352): Declared when the security of India or a part of it is threatened by war, external aggression, or armed rebellion, on the written recommendation of the Union Cabinet. (2) President's Rule / State Emergency (Article 356): Declared in a State when the President is satisfied, on receipt of a report from the Governor or otherwise, that the governance of the State cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution. (3) Financial Emergency (Article 360): Declared if the financial stability or credit of India is threatened. During National Emergency, fundamental rights may be curtailed and federal structure becomes unitary.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: Describe the election process and the primary functions of the Vice-President of India.
answer_key: Election Process: The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament (both elected and nominated members) by means of a single transferable vote system through proportional representation by secret ballot. Functions: (1) The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and presides over its proceedings, maintaining order and deciding the admissibility of questions and resolutions. (2) The Vice-President acts as the President when a vacancy occurs in the office of the President due to resignation, removal, death, or inability to discharge duties, for a maximum period of six months.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: Why is the Prime Minister considered the real executive head of the country? State any three vital roles played by the Prime Minister.
answer_key: The Prime Minister is considered the real executive head because the President acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister, and actual political and executive power is exercised by the Prime Minister. Three vital roles: (1) Link between the President and the Cabinet: The Prime Minister communicates all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to administration and proposals for legislation to the President. (2) Head of the Cabinet: The Prime Minister forms the Cabinet, distributes portfolios among ministers, can reshuffle ministries, and can ask any minister to resign. (3) Leader of the Nation and Parliament: As the leader of the majority party or coalition in the Lok Sabha, the Prime Minister guides domestic and foreign policies and steers major legislative bills.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: Explain the principle of 'Collective Responsibility' of the Council of Ministers under the Indian parliamentary system.
answer_key: Collective responsibility means that the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha for all acts and policies of the government (Article 75(3)). Key implications: (1) 'Swim together and sink together': If a vote of no-confidence is passed against one minister or if a major government bill is defeated in the Lok Sabha, the entire Council of Ministers must resign, not just the minister concerned. (2) Joint decisions: Decisions taken in Cabinet meetings are binding on all ministers, even if an individual minister disagreed during deliberations. Public dissent or criticism of government policies by a minister is not permitted.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: Distinguish between the Union Cabinet and the Council of Ministers.
answer_key: Difference between Council of Ministers and Cabinet: (1) Composition: The Council of Ministers is a large body consisting of all categories of ministers (Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers). The Cabinet is a smaller, inner core group consisting only of senior Cabinet Ministers holding important portfolios. (2) Powers and Decision-making: The Council of Ministers as a whole rarely meets. The Cabinet meets regularly as a body to determine core national policies, direct major legislation, and take crucial administrative decisions. (3) Control: The Cabinet formulates policies which are implemented by the entire Council of Ministers. Thus, the Cabinet directs and supervises the Council of Ministers.
rubric_keywords: Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, Deputy Ministers

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: Analyze the discretionary powers of the President of India. Under what circumstances can the President exercise these powers?
answer_key: Although the President is a constitutional head who acts on ministerial advice, certain discretionary powers (situational discretion) exist: (1) Appointment of Prime Minister: When no single party or coalition enjoys a clear majority in the Lok Sabha after a general election, the President exercises personal judgment in inviting a leader most likely to command a majority to form the government. (2) Dismissal of Council of Ministers: The President can dismiss the Council of Ministers if it loses the confidence of the Lok Sabha and refuses to resign. (3) Dissolution of Lok Sabha: The President may dissolve the Lok Sabha when the Council of Ministers loses majority support and advises dissolution, or when no alternative government can be formed. (4) Seeking information: The President has the right to ask the Prime Minister for information relating to administrative and legislative proposals.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: Explain the ordinance-making power of the President of India. Why is this power subject to parliamentary approval?
answer_key: Ordinance-making power (Article 123): (1) When both Houses of Parliament are not in session and the President is satisfied that immediate action is necessary, the President can promulgate ordinances having the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament. (2) Parliamentary approval: Every ordinance must be laid before both Houses of Parliament when they reassemble. It ceases to operate at the expiration of six weeks from the reassembly of Parliament, or earlier if disapproved by both Houses. (3) Why subject to approval: India follows a parliamentary democracy where law-making power rests primarily with Parliament. Ordinances are temporary executive measures designed for emergency situations when Parliament is not sitting, ensuring democratic oversight and preventing executive absolutism.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: Discuss the financial and judicial powers of the President of India.
answer_key: Financial Powers: (1) Money Bills can be introduced in the Lok Sabha only with the prior recommendation of the President. (2) The Annual Financial Statement (Union Budget) is laid before Parliament by the President's direction. (3) The President constitutes the Finance Commission every five years to recommend the distribution of tax revenues between the Centre and the States. Judicial Powers: (1) The President appoints the Chief Justice and other judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts. (2) The President possesses the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment, or to commute the sentence of any person convicted of an offense in cases involving a punishment by a Court Martial or a death sentence.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)

seed_question: If the total number of elected members in the Lok Sabha is 543 and in the Rajya Sabha is 233, calculate the total strength of the Electoral College that elects the President of India, assuming all nominated seats are vacant and all members vote.
answer_key: Step 1: Identify the components of the President's Electoral College (elected members of Lok Sabha, elected members of Rajya Sabha, and elected members of all State Legislative Assemblies). Since state MLA data is not requested or provided for calculation here, calculate based on the parliamentary component given: 543 + 233 = 776. Final Answer: 776.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
seed_question: A candidate contesting for the office of the President of India must have completed the minimum age of X years. Find the value of X.
